problems: Of the 13 findings, 11 were applied here (Algerian Sahara 1903 and AOF 1905 re-dating; Guinea 1884 keyframe; Liberia gains 1892-12 and 1907-09; Wadai War events and wars[]; Dahomey 1890 and 1892-1894 events with month 1 and the First Franco-Dahomean War; Porto-Novo 1863-1865; Dar al Kuti 1912 gain; Tunisia occupation 1942-11 to 1943-05; Djibouti occupation by british-africa; gains from german-africa for the 1919 and 1922 mandates; the Libyan block dropped) and 2 were already applied by the reviewer (counterpart slugs, the Algerian War clip). No finding was left undone; judgement calls are in the notes file.

Disagreements with the reviewer's text: none on substance. The Libyan block is dropped as asked, but Cliopatria's 1920 drop coincides with the Franco-Italian boundary treaty of 12 September 1919 (Algeria-Libya border page), so the block may reflect a French claim; restore it only if a page shows French posts there. The Neukamerun gain is confidence 2 because the Kamerun campaign page is silent on its fate after the war.

The Djibouti and Tunisia occupation events name the occupier as the counterpart (british-africa, nazi-germany) although the land is french-africa's, as the review asked; the schema text reads the other way round, so the rendering agent should check the direction convention.

The repair opened nine pages beyond the 14-page budget (Wadai War, two Franco-Dahomean wars, Porto-Novo, two Liberia border pages, Tunisia campaign, Algeria-Libya border, Ghat) at the reviewer's request.

Mirrors missing in other dossiers: british-africa (Djibouti 1942-1943), german-africa (not written), italian-africa and nazi-germany and free-french (eu-21, not written), dar-al-kuti (1897 vassal_start), merina-kingdom (1895 vassal_start), sokoto-caliphate (no french-africa event), kingdom-of-porto-novo (1863 loss versus a protectorate tint).
